cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: The NEA (Non-Exam Assessment) is a practical project that typically contributes 25-40% of the GCSE grade.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: AQA Engineering NEA (40%): students produce engineering drawings, a working prototype and a portfolio.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: WJEC Eduqas has two NEA units: Manufacturing Engineering Products (Unit 1) and Designing Engineering Products (Unit 2).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: The portfolio must show clear progression through research, design, planning, manufacture and evaluation stages.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Research should be relevant and specific: investigate existing products, materials, processes and user needs.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Design development shows how ideas evolve from initial sketches through to the final chosen solution with justification.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Manufacturing plans list operations, tools, materials and safety precautions in the correct sequence.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Quality of manufacture is assessed: accuracy, finish, functionality and adherence to the plan.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Testing and evaluation compare the finished product against the specification; identify improvements.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Annotation on drawings and photographs explains decisions - do not leave the examiner to guess your reasoning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: Time management is critical: allocate sufficient time for each stage and meet all deadlines.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Practical Assessment Technique
cards.back: The portfolio should be concise, focused and well-organised - quality of evidence matters more than quantity of pages.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — practical assessment technique?
cards.back: 1. For Practical Assessment Technique questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Practical Assessment Technique through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
A student's NEA project is to design and manufacture a wall-mounted tool holder for a home workshop. Write a suitable specification with at least six measurable criteria. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of practical assessment technique, including materials, manufacturing processes and engineering systems relevant to AQA 8852 & WJEC Eduqas 5799QA. AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of practical assessment technique to analyse, design and manufacture engineering solutions. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate engineer
